rationale: Reject the queued ADD_PENDING_TRANSACTION action and correct the existing PUC Transmission LP record. Axium's September 25, 2024 release states that a managed fund had acquired an 80% equity interest, and the Ontario Energy Board's December 31, 2024 ownership schedule places that interest beneath Axium Infrastructure Canada II Limited Partnership through Axium TransCo GP Inc. and Axium TransCo LP. PUC Inc. retains the 20% balance. The May 2024 municipal reference to a later project close concerns scheduled equity funding for construction, not an unclosed Axium acquisition. Remove the unsupported generic AxInfra Fund I-IV / Axium Managed Funds attribution, preserve AIC II / Axium TransCo as the disclosed vehicle chain, add PUC Inc. as an unlinked municipal co-owner, and create no pending transaction. The OEB granted leave to construct on August 27, 2024 and issued licence ET-2021-0088 on April 10, 2025 after its October 2021 conditional approval. Current company materials report a C$230 million, two-400-MVA-circuit project targeting Q1 2028 completion. No later sale, ownership transfer, signed pending exit, cancellation, abandonment or licence revocation was identified through August 18, 2026.

beforeImage.name: PUC Transmission LP
beforeImage.description: PUC Transmission LP is a regulated transmission development platform in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. The company is developing a 230 kV transmission line and transformer station intended to connect new industrial and regional loads, including Algoma Steel’s electric arc furnace project. Its operating model is asset-heavy and regulated, with cost recovery and allowed returns governed by Ontario’s utility regulatory framework rather than merchant power exposure. Public materials describe the project as approximately 10 kilometers of double-circuit line and a new 230 kV station, with commercial operation expected by the end of 2027. PUC Transmission was incorporated in 2021, and Axium acquired an 80% equity interest in 2024 while the Public Utility Commission of Sault Ste. Marie retained 20%.

afterImage.name: PUC Transmission LP
afterImage.description: PUC Transmission LP is an Ontario regulated transmitter developing, financing, constructing and operating Tagona West Transformer Station and an approximately 10 route-kilometre, dual-circuit 230 kV transmission line in Sault Ste. Marie. The approximately C$230 million project will provide about 300 MW of new load to Algoma Steel's electric-arc-furnace operations while strengthening regional reliability and capacity. The line comprises approximately 20 circuit-kilometres across two 400 MVA circuits. Axium Infrastructure holds 80% through the disclosed Axium Infrastructure Canada II Limited Partnership / Axium TransCo chain, while PUC Inc. retains 20%. The OEB granted leave to construct on August 27, 2024 and issued electricity transmission licence ET-2021-0088 on April 10, 2025. Current company materials target construction completion in Q1 2028 and energization in January 2028. No later ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.
